claim: evalSubquery merges the subquery's SamplesRead into the parent, but the materialized points are then re-counted by the matrix-selector range-eval path at engine.go:2184, so every subquery's reads are counted twice; SamplesRead can exceed TotalSamples.
raw: subquery samples are counted twice in `SamplesRead`

claim: stats.NewChildWithStepTracking calls InitStepTracking, eagerly allocating two []int64 of (queryRange + subqueryRange)/subqueryStep before the subquery runs, so query.max-samples cannot stop it; the subquery step is caller-controlled down to 1ms, making the allocation unbounded (55 MiB measured for count_over_time(m[1h:1ms]) with MaxSamples=10).
raw: every subquery now eagerly allocates 16 bytes per subquery step, before any sample limit applies

claim: The ~1100 new table-test lines encode the double-counted values (comments say `// subquery + outer`), so the subquery portion of the table passes because of the defect and would fail once it is fixed; no case asserts SamplesRead <= TotalSamples.
raw: the new test cases encode the double-counted values, so they cannot fail for the defect

claim: Both docs pages state two false properties of samplesRead: that it equals totalQueryableSamples for non-range-vector queries (measured 4 vs 2), and that it is a count of samples read (I/O) — instant vector selectors increment once per step with no de-duplication of lookback-overlapped re-reads.
raw: both docs pages state two properties of `samplesRead` that the implementation does not have

claim: IncrementSamplesReadAtStep and IncrementSamplesReadAtTimestamp silently skip out-of-range indices while their pre-existing siblings panic, and the scalar SamplesRead is incremented before the guard, so a bad index silently yields SamplesRead != sum(SamplesReadPerStep); IncrementSamplesReadAtStep also lacks the i >= 0 check its sibling has.
raw: the new increment helpers silently drop out-of-range steps where their siblings panic

claim: The outer-step index mixes sources: the base comes from the evaluator (ev.startTimestamp) while the stride comes from the stats object (ev.samplesStats.Interval); the correct partner for ev.startTimestamp is ev.interval, so the pairing is fragile though traced equal on every reachable path.

countSamplesAfter scans both floats and histograms front-to-back, but the slices are time-ordered with new points at the tail, so a reverse scan with an early break would be O(new) instead of O(window).
NewChildWithStepTracking is a package function while NewChild is a method; that asymmetry is the only reason the StepTrackingEnabled() accessor had to be added.
raw: `NewChildWithStepTracking` is a package function while `NewChild` is a method (Consistency)
